author: Janelle Faignant Correspondent
title: Discover Halloween festivities all month at Rutland Free Library | Local News | rutlandherald.com
text:
An escape room mystery, a horror makeup tutorial for teens, and Halloween Bingo are just some of the spooky things happening at Rutland Free Library this month — and it starts with its first-ever Halloween Heist Escape Room on Monday, Oct. 13.
The Story: The All Hallows Key, which holds the spirit of Halloween, is missing, and Halloween is in danger of fading away if the key isn’t found before midnight. Time is running out — there’s only an hour to find the clues and catch the thief.
The Plot: Puzzles, riddles and hidden clues are waiting to be found like a scavenger hunt to save Halloween.
Grab your friends and family and sign up for a spot in the escape room during three different time slots: 10 a.m., 1 p.m., and 4 p.m. There are six spots available for each session, and you might be playing with people you don’t know. Pay close attention to the time slot for which you are registered. This event is for ages 8 through 18, and no parents, guardians, or adults are allowed in the escape room.
“(Young Adult Librarian) Tiaunna (Leddick) and I had wanted to do an escape room for a while,” said Children’s Services Librarian Amanda Münch. “In 2024, when the summer reading theme was ‘Adventure,’ we decided to try an escape room. We found a website that offered pre-made games with pieces that could be printed off. For this Halloween-themed one, we are using a different kit from the same company. We make sure to test the game ahead of time and make any tweaks that we need to.”
“Amanda was the genius who decided the Small Meeting Room was perfect for a temporary escape room,” said Leddick. “We buy pre-made kits from companies that specialize in this type of thing.”
“We keep the age range wide because that’s typically what the games are suggested for,” Münch said. “We then make decisions based on the age ranges we serve. In this case, Tiaunna and I serve birth (through) teen. We are working on offering more for the 8-12 range, and this is one particular instance where we feel OK merging them with the teens, as long as we don’t go too young. This is the same reason we’ve decided to exclude adults for this round: We want to make sure these kids have the space they need to be themselves.”
“Amanda and I do test each escape room before unleashing it on the public — the one we’re doing on Monday is actually the second one we’ve bought,” Leddick said. “We had gotten an ‘Escape the Witch Trial’ box, but we couldn’t solve it without lots of hints, and it took over an hour and a half.”
“Family-friendly, puzzle-fest, story-driven, and immersive” were common words used to describe it online, and one reviewer said the Halloween Heist was “like a treasure trail with immersive actors, small puzzles, hunts and other immersive elements.” Another reviewer said, “The game is a complete delight, that’s chock-a-block with puzzles. We’d happily turn back around and do the whole thing again.”
“Both Tiaunna and I have done other Halloween-themed programs in the past and are offering others this year as well,” Münch added.
Halloween Bingo takes place on Wednesday, Oct. 29, for families and kids up to age 12. A Fright Night with storyteller Simon Brooks takes place Tuesday, Oct. 28. And both the Horror Movie Night for teens and Horror Makeup/SFX for teens are back by popular demand on Tuesday, Oct. 21.
“We also have the Great Pumpkin Costume Contest, which is … very much a Halloween-inspired program,” Münch said.
For more details and to register, go to www.rutlandfree.org/calendar-events.
Disclosure: The author is a part-time employee of the Rutland Free Library.
